text_en: The song of songs, which {is} Solomon's.
text_pt: cântico dos cânticos, que é de Salomão.
text_el: ᾆσμα ᾀσμάτων ὅ ἐστιν τῷ Σαλωμων

text_en: Let him kiss me with the kiss of his mouth: for your breasts are better than wine,
text_la: Sponsa. Osculetur me osculo oris sui; quia meliora sunt ubera tua vino,
text_pt: Beije-me ele com os beijos da sua boca; porque melhor é o teu amor do que o vinho.
text_el: φιλησάτω με ἀπὸ φιλημάτων στόματος αὐτοῦ ὅτι ἀγαθοὶ μαστοί σου ὑπὲρ οἶνον

text_en: smelling sweet of the best ointments . Your name is as oil poured out: therefore young maidens have loved you.
text_la: fragrantia unguentis optimis. Oleum effusum nomen tuum; ideo adolescentulæ dilexerunt te.
text_pt: Suave é o aroma dos teus ungüentos; como o ungüento derramado é o teu nome; por isso as virgens te amam.
text_el: καὶ ὀσμὴ μύρων σου ὑπὲρ πάντα τὰ ἀρώματα μύρον ἐκκενωθὲν ὄνομά σου διὰ τοῦτο νεάνιδες ἠγάπησάν σε

text_en: Draw me: we will run after you to the odour of your ointments . The king has brought me into his storerooms: we will be glad and rejoice in you, remembering your breasts more than wine: the righteous love you.
text_la: Chorus Adolescentularum. Trahe me, post te curremus in odorem unguentorum tuorum. Introduxit me rex in cellaria sua; exsultabimus et lætabimur in te, memores uberum tuorum super vinum. Recti diligunt te.
text_pt: Leva-me tu; correremos após ti. O rei me introduziu nas suas câmaras; em ti nos regozijaremos e nos alegraremos; do teu amor nos lembraremos, mais do que do vinho; os retos te amam.
text_el: εἵλκυσάν σε ὀπίσω σου εἰς ὀσμὴν μύρων σου δραμοῦμεν εἰσήνεγκέν με ὁ βασιλεὺς εἰς τὸ ταμίειον αὐτοῦ ἀγαλλιασώμεθα καὶ εὐφρανθῶμεν ἐν σοί ἀγαπήσομεν μαστούς σου ὑπὲρ οἶνον εὐθύτης ἠγάπησέν σε

text_en: I am black but beautiful, O you daughters of Jerusalem , as the tents of Cedar , as the curtains of Solomon .
text_la: Sponsa. Nigra sum, sed formosa, filiæ Jerusalem, sicut tabernacula Cedar, sicut pelles Salomonis.
text_pt: Eu sou morena, porém formosa, ó filhas de Jerusalém, como as tendas de Quedar, como as cortinas de Salomão.
text_el: μέλαινά εἰμι καὶ καλή θυγατέρες Ιερουσαλημ ὡς σκηνώματα Κηδαρ ὡς δέρρεις Σαλωμων

text_en: Do not consider me that I am brown, because the sun has altered my colour: the sons of my mother have fought against me, they have made me the keeper in the vineyards: my vineyard I have not kept.
text_la: Nolite me considerare quod fusca sim, quia decoloravit me sol. Filii matris meæ pugnaverunt contra me; posuerunt me custodem in vineis : vineam meam non custodivi.
text_pt: Não olheis para o eu ser morena, porque o sol resplandeceu sobre mim; os filhos de minha mãe indignaram-se contra mim, puseram-me por guarda das vinhas; a minha vinha, porém, não guardei.
text_el: μὴ βλέψητέ με ὅτι ἐγώ εἰμι μεμελανωμένη ὅτι παρέβλεψέν με ὁ ἥλιος υἱοὶ μητρός μου ἐμαχέσαντο ἐν ἐμοί ἔθεντό με φυλάκισσαν ἐν ἀμπελῶσιν ἀμπελῶνα ἐμὸν οὐκ ἐφύλαξα

text_en: Show me, O you whom my soul loves , where you feed, where you lie in the midday, lest I begin to wander after the flocks of your companions.
text_la: Indica mihi, quem diligit anima mea, ubi pascas, ubi cubes in meridie, ne vagari incipiam post greges sodalium tuorum.
text_pt: Dize-me, ó tu, a quem ama a minha alma: Onde apascentas o teu rebanho, onde o fazes descansar ao meio-dia; pois por que razão seria eu como a que anda errante junto aos rebanhos de teus companheiros?
text_el: ἀπάγγειλόν μοι ὃν ἠγάπησεν ἡ ψυχή μου ποῦ ποιμαίνεις ποῦ κοιτάζεις ἐν μεσημβρίᾳ μήποτε γένωμαι ὡς περιβαλλομένη ἐπ' ἀγέλαις ἑταίρων σου

text_en: If you know not yourself, O fairest among women , go forth, and follow after the steps of the flocks, and feed your kids beside the tents of the shepherds.
text_la: Sponsus. Si ignoras te, o pulcherrima inter mulieres, egredere, et abi post vestigia gregum, et pasce hædos tuos juxta tabernacula pastorum.
text_pt: Se tu não o sabes, ó mais formosa entre as mulheres, sai-te pelas pisadas do rebanho, e apascenta as tuas cabras junto às moradas dos pastores.
text_el: ἐὰν μὴ γνῷς σεαυτήν ἡ καλὴ ἐν γυναιξίν ἔξελθε σὺ ἐν πτέρναις τῶν ποιμνίων καὶ ποίμαινε τὰς ἐρίφους σου ἐπὶ σκηνώμασιν τῶν ποιμένων

text_en: To my company of horsemen, in Pharao's chariots, have I likened you, O my love .
text_la: Equitatui meo in curribus Pharaonis assimilavi te, amica mea.
text_pt: Às éguas dos carros de Faraó te comparo, ó meu amor.
text_el: τῇ ἵππῳ μου ἐν ἅρμασιν Φαραω ὡμοίωσά σε ἡ πλησίον μου

text_en: Your cheeks are beautiful as the turtledove's, your neck as jewels .
text_la: Pulchræ sunt genæ tuæ sicut turturis; collum tuum sicut monilia.
text_pt: Formosas são as tuas faces entre os teus enfeites, o teu pescoço com os colares.
text_el: τί ὡραιώθησαν σιαγόνες σου ὡς τρυγόνες τράχηλός σου ὡς ὁρμίσκοι

text_en: We will make you chains of gold, inlaid with silver.
text_la: Murenulas aureas faciemus tibi, vermiculatas argento.
text_pt: Enfeites de ouro te faremos, com incrustações de prata.
text_el: ὁμοιώματα χρυσίου ποιήσομέν σοι μετὰ στιγμάτων τοῦ ἀργυρίου

text_en: While the king was at his repose, my spikenard sent forth the odour thereof.
text_la: Sponsa. Dum esset rex in accubitu suo, nardus mea dedit odorem suum.
text_pt: Enquanto o rei está assentado à sua mesa, o meu nardo exala o seu perfume.
text_el: ἕως οὗ ὁ βασιλεὺς ἐν ἀνακλίσει αὐτοῦ νάρδος μου ἔδωκεν ὀσμὴν αὐτοῦ

text_en: A bundle of myrrh is my beloved to me, he shall abide between my breasts.
text_la: Fasciculus myrrhæ dilectus meus mihi; inter ubera mea commorabitur.
text_pt: O meu amado é para mim como um ramalhete de mirra, posto entre os meus seios.
text_el: ἀπόδεσμος τῆς στακτῆς ἀδελφιδός μου ἐμοί ἀνὰ μέσον τῶν μαστῶν μου αὐλισθήσεται

text_en: A cluster of cypress my love is to me, in the vineyards of Engaddi .
text_la: Botrus cypri dilectus meus mihi in vineis Engaddi.
text_pt: Como um ramalhete de hena nas vinhas de En-Gedi, é para mim o meu amado.
text_el: βότρυς τῆς κύπρου ἀδελφιδός μου ἐμοὶ ἐν ἀμπελῶσιν Εγγαδδι

text_en: Behold you are fair, O my love , behold you are fair, your eyes are as those of doves.
text_la: Sponsus. Ecce tu pulchra es, amica mea! ecce tu pulchra es! Oculi tui columbarum.
text_pt: Eis que és formosa, ó meu amor, eis que és formosa; os teus olhos são como os das pombas.
text_el: ἰδοὺ εἶ καλή ἡ πλησίον μου ἰδοὺ εἶ καλή ὀφθαλμοί σου περιστεραί

text_en: Behold you are fair, my beloved, and comely. Our bed is flourishing.
text_la: Sponsa. Ecce tu pulcher es, dilecte mi, et decorus! Lectulus noster floridus.
text_pt: Eis que és formoso, ó amado meu, e também amável; o nosso leito é verde.
text_el: ἰδοὺ εἶ καλός ὁ ἀδελφιδός μου καί γε ὡραῖος πρὸς κλίνη ἡμῶν σύσκιος

text_en: The beams of our houses are of cedar , our rafters of cypress trees.
text_la: Tigna domorum nostrarum cedrina, laquearia nostra cypressina.
text_pt: As traves da nossa casa são de cedro, as nossas varandas de cipreste.
text_el: δοκοὶ οἴκων ἡμῶν κέδροι φατνώματα ἡμῶν κυπάρισσοι

text_en: I am the flower of the field, and the lily of the valleys.
text_la: Ego flos campi, et lilium convallium.
text_pt: Eu sou a rosa de Sarom, o lírio dos vales.
text_el: ἐγὼ ἄνθος τοῦ πεδίου κρίνον τῶν κοιλάδων

text_en: As the lily among thorns, so is my love among the daughters.
text_la: Sponsus. Sicut lilium inter spinas, sic amica mea inter filias.
text_pt: Qual o lírio entre os espinhos, tal é meu amor entre as filhas.
text_el: ὡς κρίνον ἐν μέσῳ ἀκανθῶν οὕτως ἡ πλησίον μου ἀνὰ μέσον τῶν θυγατέρων

text_en: As the apple tree among the trees of the woods, so is my beloved among the sons. I sat down under his shadow, whom I desired: and his fruit was sweet to my palate.
text_la: Sponsa. Sicut malus inter ligna silvarum, sic dilectus meus inter filios. Sub umbra illius quem desideraveram sedi, et fructus ejus dulcis gutturi meo.
text_pt: Qual a macieira entre as árvores do bosque, tal é o meu amado entre os filhos;desejo muito a sua sombra, e debaixo dela me assento;e o seu fruto é doce ao meu paladar.
text_el: ὡς μῆλον ἐν τοῖς ξύλοις τοῦ δρυμοῦ οὕτως ἀδελφιδός μου ἀνὰ μέσον τῶν υἱῶν ἐν τῇ σκιᾷ αὐτοῦ ἐπεθύμησα καὶ ἐκάθισα καὶ καρπὸς αὐτοῦ γλυκὺς ἐν λάρυγγί μου

text_en: He brought me into the cellar of wine, he set in order charity in me.
text_la: Introduxit me in cellam vinariam; ordinavit in me caritatem.
text_pt: Levou-me à casa do banquete, e o seu estandarte sobre mim era o amor.
text_el: εἰσαγάγετέ με εἰς οἶκον τοῦ οἴνου τάξατε ἐπ' ἐμὲ ἀγάπην

text_en: Stay me up with flowers, compass me about with apples: because I languish with love .
text_la: Fulcite me floribus, stipate me malis, quia amore langueo.
text_pt: Sustentai-me com passas, confortai-me com maçãs, porque desfaleço de amor.
text_el: στηρίσατέ με ἐν ἀμόραις στοιβάσατέ με ἐν μήλοις ὅτι τετρωμένη ἀγάπης ἐγώ

text_en: His left hand is under my head, and his right hand shall embrace me.
text_la: Læva ejus sub capite meo, et dextera illius amplexabitur me.
text_pt: A sua mão esquerda esteja debaixo da minha cabeça, e a sua mão direita me abrace.
text_el: εὐώνυμος αὐτοῦ ὑπὸ τὴν κεφαλήν μου καὶ ἡ δεξιὰ αὐτοῦ περιλήμψεταί με

text_en: I adjure you, O you daughters of Jerusalem , by the roes, and the harts of the field, that you stir not up, nor make the beloved to awake, till she please.
text_la: Sponsus. Adjuro vos, filiæ Jerusalem, per capreas cervosque camporum, ne suscitetis, neque evigilare faciatis dilectam, quoadusque ipsa velit.
text_pt: Conjuro-vos, ó filhas de Jerusalém, pelas gazelas e cervas do campo, que não acordeis nem desperteis o meu amor, até que queira.
text_el: ὥρκισα ὑμᾶς θυγατέρες Ιερουσαλημ ἐν ταῖς δυνάμεσιν καὶ ἐν ταῖς ἰσχύσεσιν τοῦ ἀγροῦ ἐὰν ἐγείρητε καὶ ἐξεγείρητε τὴν ἀγάπην ἕως οὗ θελήσῃ

text_en: The voice of my beloved, behold he comes leaping upon the mountains, skipping over the hills.
text_la: Sponsa. Vox dilecti mei; ecce iste venit, saliens in montibus, transiliens colles.
text_pt: Esta é a voz do meu amado; ei-lo aí, que já vem saltando sobre os montes, pulando sobre os outeiros.
text_el: φωνὴ ἀδελφιδοῦ μου ἰδοὺ οὗτος ἥκει πηδῶν ἐπὶ τὰ ὄρη διαλλόμενος ἐπὶ τοὺς βουνούς

text_en: My beloved is like a roe, or a young hart. Behold he stands behind our wall, looking through the windows, looking through the lattices.
text_la: Similis est dilectus meus capreæ, hinnuloque cervorum. En ipse stat post parietem nostrum, respiciens per fenestras, prospiciens per cancellos.
text_pt: O meu amado é semelhante ao gamo, ou ao filho do veado; eis que está detrás da nossa parede, olhando pelas janelas, espreitando pelas grades.
text_el: ὅμοιός ἐστιν ἀδελφιδός μου τῇ δορκάδι ἢ νεβρῷ ἐλάφων ἐπὶ τὰ ὄρη Βαιθηλ ἰδοὺ οὗτος ἕστηκεν ὀπίσω τοῦ τοίχου ἡμῶν παρακύπτων διὰ τῶν θυρίδων ἐκκύπτων διὰ τῶν δικτύων

text_en: Behold my beloved speaks to me: Arise, make haste, my love , my dove , my beautiful one, and come.
text_la: En dilectus meus loquitur mihi. Sponsus. Surge, propera, amica mea, columba mea, formosa mea, et veni :
text_pt: O meu amado fala e me diz: Levanta-te, meu amor, formosa minha, e vem.
text_el: ἀποκρίνεται ἀδελφιδός μου καὶ λέγει μοι ἀνάστα ἐλθέ ἡ πλησίον μου καλή μου περιστερά μου

text_en: For winter is now past, the rain is over and gone.
text_la: jam enim hiems transiit; imber abiit, et recessit.
text_pt: Porque eis que passou o inverno; a chuva cessou, e se foi;
text_el: ὅτι ἰδοὺ ὁ χειμὼν παρῆλθεν ὁ ὑετὸς ἀπῆλθεν ἐπορεύθη ἑαυτῷ

text_en: The flowers have appeared in our land, the time of pruning has come: the voice of the turtle is heard in our land:
text_la: Flores apparuerunt in terra nostra; tempus putationis advenit : vox turturis audita est in terra nostra;
text_pt: Aparecem as flores na terra, o tempo de cantar chega, e a voz da rola ouve-se em nossa terra.
text_el: τὰ ἄνθη ὤφθη ἐν τῇ γῇ καιρὸς τῆς τομῆς ἔφθακεν φωνὴ τοῦ τρυγόνος ἠκούσθη ἐν τῇ γῇ ἡμῶν

text_en: The fig tree has put forth her green figs: the vines in flower yield their sweet smell. Arise, my love , my beautiful one, and come:
text_la: ficus protulit grossos suos; vineæ florentes dederunt odorem suum. Surge, amica mea, speciosa mea, et veni :
text_pt: A figueira já deu os seus figos verdes, e as vides em flor exalam o seu aroma; levanta-te, meu amor, formosa minha, e vem.
text_el: ἡ συκῆ ἐξήνεγκεν ὀλύνθους αὐτῆς αἱ ἄμπελοι κυπρίζουσιν ἔδωκαν ὀσμήν ἀνάστα ἐλθέ ἡ πλησίον μου καλή μου περιστερά μου

text_en: My dove in the clefts of the rock, in the hollow places of the wall, show me your face, let your voice sound in my ears: for your voice is sweet, and your face comely.
text_la: columba mea, in foraminibus petræ, in caverna maceriæ, ostende mihi faciem tuam, sonet vox tua in auribus meis : vox enim tua dulcis, et facies tua decora.
text_pt: Pomba minha, que andas pelas fendas das penhas, no oculto das ladeiras, mostra-me a tua face, faze-me ouvir a tua voz, porque a tua voz é doce, e a tua face graciosa.
text_el: καὶ ἐλθὲ σύ περιστερά μου ἐν σκέπῃ τῆς πέτρας ἐχόμενα τοῦ προτειχίσματος δεῖξόν μοι τὴν ὄψιν σου καὶ ἀκούτισόν με τὴν φωνήν σου ὅτι ἡ φωνή σου ἡδεῖα καὶ ἡ ὄψις σου ὡραία

text_en: Catch us the little foxes that destroy the vines: for our vineyard has flourished.
text_la: Sponsa. Capite nobis vulpes parvulas quæ demoliuntur vineas : nam vinea nostra floruit.
text_pt: Apanhai-nos as raposas, as raposinhas, que fazem mal às vinhas, porque as nossas vinhas estão em flor.
text_el: πιάσατε ἡμῖν ἀλώπεκας μικροὺς ἀφανίζοντας ἀμπελῶνας καὶ αἱ ἄμπελοι ἡμῶν κυπρίζουσιν

text_en: My beloved to me, and I to him who feeds among the lilies,
text_la: Dilectus meus mihi, et ego illi, qui pascitur inter lilia,
text_pt: O meu amado é meu, e eu sou dele; ele apascenta o seu rebanho entre os lírios.
text_el: ἀδελφιδός μου ἐμοί κἀγὼ αὐτῷ ὁ ποιμαίνων ἐν τοῖς κρίνοις

text_en: till the day break, and the shadows retire. Return: be like, my beloved, to a roe, or to a young hart upon the mountains of Bether.
text_la: donec aspiret dies, et inclinentur umbræ. Revertere; similis esto, dilecte mi, capreæ, hinnuloque cervorum super montes Bether.
text_pt: Até que refresque o dia, e fujam as sombras, volta, amado meu; faze-te semelhante ao gamo ou ao filho dos veados sobre os montes de Beter.
text_el: ἕως οὗ διαπνεύσῃ ἡ ἡμέρα καὶ κινηθῶσιν αἱ σκιαί ἀπόστρεψον ὁμοιώθητι σύ ἀδελφιδέ μου τῷ δόρκωνι ἢ νεβρῷ ἐλάφων ἐπὶ ὄρη κοιλωμάτων

text_en: In my bed by night I sought him whom my soul loves : I sought him, and found him not.
text_la: In lectulo meo, per noctes, quæsivi quem diligit anima mea : quæsivi illum, et non inveni.
text_pt: De noite, em minha cama, busquei aquele a quem ama a minha alma; busquei-o, e não o achei.
text_el: ἐπὶ κοίτην μου ἐν νυξὶν ἐζήτησα ὃν ἠγάπησεν ἡ ψυχή μου ἐζήτησα αὐτὸν καὶ οὐχ εὗρον αὐτόν ἐκάλεσα αὐτόν καὶ οὐχ ὑπήκουσέν μου

text_en: I will rise, and will go about the city: in the streets and the broad ways I will seek him whom my soul loves : I sought him, and I found him not.
text_la: Surgam, et circuibo civitatem : per vicos et plateas quæram quem diligit anima mea : quæsivi illum, et non inveni.
text_pt: Levantar-me-ei, pois, e rodearei a cidade;pelas ruas e pelas praças buscarei aquele a quem ama a minha alma;busquei-o, e não o achei.
text_el: ἀναστήσομαι δὴ καὶ κυκλώσω ἐν τῇ πόλει ἐν ταῖς ἀγοραῖς καὶ ἐν ταῖς πλατείαις καὶ ζητήσω ὃν ἠγάπησεν ἡ ψυχή μου ἐζήτησα αὐτὸν καὶ οὐχ εὗρον αὐτόν

text_en: The watchmen who keep the city, found me: Have you seen him, whom my soul loves ?
text_la: Invenerunt me vigiles qui custodiunt civitatem : Num quem diligit anima mea vidistis?
text_pt: Acharam-me os guardas, que rondavam pela cidade;eu lhes perguntei: Vistes aquele a quem ama a minha alma?
text_el: εὕροσάν με οἱ τηροῦντες οἱ κυκλοῦντες ἐν τῇ πόλει μὴ ὃν ἠγάπησεν ἡ ψυχή μου εἴδετε

text_en: When I had a little passed by them, I found him whom my soul loves : I held him: and I will not let him go, till I bring him into my mother's house, and into the chamber of her that bore me.
text_la: Paululum cum pertransissem eos, inveni quem diligit anima mea : tenui eum, nec dimittam, donec introducam illum in domum matris meæ, et in cubiculum genetricis meæ.
text_pt: Apartando-me eu um pouco deles, logo achei aquele a quem ama a minha alma; agarrei-me a ele, e não o larguei, até que o introduzi em casa de minha mãe, na câmara daquela que me gerou.
text_el: ὡς μικρὸν ὅτε παρῆλθον ἀπ' αὐτῶν ἕως οὗ εὗρον ὃν ἠγάπησεν ἡ ψυχή μου ἐκράτησα αὐτὸν καὶ οὐκ ἀφήσω αὐτόν ἕως οὗ εἰσήγαγον αὐτὸν εἰς οἶκον μητρός μου καὶ εἰς ταμίειον τῆς συλλαβούσης με

text_en: I adjure you, O daughters of Jerusalem , by the roes and the harts of the fields, that you stir not up, nor awake my beloved, till she please.
text_la: Sponsus. Adjuro vos, filiæ Jerusalem, per capreas cervosque camporum, ne suscitetis, neque evigilare faciatis dilectam, donec ipsa velit.
text_pt: Conjuro-vos, ó filhas de Jerusalém, pelas gazelas e cervas do campo, que não acordeis, nem desperteis o meu amor, até que queira.
text_el: ὥρκισα ὑμᾶς θυγατέρες Ιερουσαλημ ἐν ταῖς δυνάμεσιν καὶ ἐν ταῖς ἰσχύσεσιν τοῦ ἀγροῦ ἐὰν ἐγείρητε καὶ ἐξεγείρητε τὴν ἀγάπην ἕως ἂν θελήσῃ

text_en: Who is she that goes up by the desert , as a pillar of smoke of aromatical spices, of myrrh, and frankincense, and of all the powders of the perfumer?
text_la: Chorus. Quæ est ista quæ ascendit per desertum sicut virgula fumi ex aromatibus myrrhæ, et thuris, et universi pulveris pigmentarii?
text_pt: Quem é esta que sobe do deserto, como colunas de fumaça, perfumada de mirra, de incenso, e de todos os pós dos mercadores?
text_el: τίς αὕτη ἡ ἀναβαίνουσα ἀπὸ τῆς ἐρήμου ὡς στελέχη καπνοῦ τεθυμιαμένη σμύρναν καὶ λίβανον ἀπὸ πάντων κονιορτῶν μυρεψοῦ

text_en: Behold threescore valiant ones of the most valiant of Israel , surrounded the bed of Solomon ?
text_la: En lectulum Salomonis sexaginta fortes ambiunt ex fortissimis Israël,
text_pt: Eis que é a liteira de Salomão; sessenta valentes estão ao redor dela, dos valentes de Israel;
text_el: ἰδοὺ ἡ κλίνη τοῦ Σαλωμων ἑξήκοντα δυνατοὶ κύκλῳ αὐτῆς ἀπὸ δυνατῶν Ισραηλ

text_en: All holding swords, and most expert in war : every man's sword upon his thigh, because of fears in the night.
text_la: omnes tenentes gladios, et ad bella doctissimi : uniuscujusque ensis super femur suum propter timores nocturnos.
text_pt: Todos armados de espadas, destros na guerra; cada um com a sua espada à cinta por causa dos temores noturnos.
text_el: πάντες κατέχοντες ῥομφαίαν δεδιδαγμένοι πόλεμον ἀνὴρ ῥομφαία αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ μηρὸν αὐτοῦ ἀπὸ θάμβους ἐν νυξίν

text_en: King Solomon has made him a litter of the wood of Libanus :
text_la: Ferculum fecit sibi rex Salomon de lignis Libani;
text_pt: O rei Salomão fez para si uma carruagem de madeira do Líbano.
text_el: φορεῖον ἐποίησεν ἑαυτῷ ὁ βασιλεὺς Σαλωμων ἀπὸ ξύλων τοῦ Λιβάνου

text_en: The pillars thereof he made of silver, the seat of gold, the going up of purple: the midst he covered with charity for the daughters of Jerusalem .
text_la: columnas ejus fecit argenteas, reclinatorium aureum, ascensum purpureum; media caritate constravit, propter filias Jerusalem.
text_pt: Fez-lhe as colunas de prata, o estrado de ouro, o assento de púrpura, o interior revestido com amor, pelas filhas de Jerusalém.
text_el: στύλους αὐτοῦ ἐποίησεν ἀργύριον καὶ ἀνάκλιτον αὐτοῦ χρύσεον ἐπίβασις αὐτοῦ πορφυρᾶ ἐντὸς αὐτοῦ λιθόστρωτον ἀγάπην ἀπὸ θυγατέρων Ιερουσαλημ

text_en: Go forth, you daughters of Sion, and see King Solomon in the diadem, wherewith his mother crowned him in the day of the joy of his heart.
text_la: Egredimini et videte, filiæ Sion, regem Salomonem in diademate quo coronavit illum mater sua in die desponsationis illius, et in die lætitiæ cordis ejus.
text_pt: Saí, ó filhas de Sião, e contemplai ao rei Salomão com a coroa com que o coroou sua mãe no dia do seu desposório e no dia do júbilo do seu coração.
text_el: ἐξέλθατε καὶ ἴδετε ἐν τῷ βασιλεῖ Σαλωμων ἐν τῷ στεφάνῳ ᾧ ἐστεφάνωσεν αὐτὸν ἡ μήτηρ αὐτοῦ ἐν ἡμέρᾳ νυμφεύσεως αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐν ἡμέρᾳ εὐφροσύνης καρδίας αὐτοῦ

text_en: How beautiful are you, my love , how beautiful are you! your eyes are doves' eyes, besides what is hid within. Your hair is as flocks of goats, which come up from mount Galaad.
text_la: Sponsus. Quam pulchra es, amica mea! quam pulchra es! Oculi tui columbarum, absque eo quod intrinsecus latet. Capilli tui sicut greges caprarum quæ ascenderunt de monte Galaad.
text_pt: Eis que és formosa, meu amor, eis que és formosa; os teus olhos são como os das pombas entre as tuas tranças; o teu cabelo é como o rebanho de cabras que pastam no monte de Gileade.
text_el: ἰδοὺ εἶ καλή ἡ πλησίον μου ἰδοὺ εἶ καλή ὀφθαλμοί σου περιστεραὶ ἐκτὸς τῆς σιωπήσεώς σου τρίχωμά σου ὡς ἀγέλαι τῶν αἰγῶν αἳ ἀπεκαλύφθησαν ἀπὸ τοῦ Γαλααδ

text_en: Your teeth as flocks of sheep, that are shorn, which come up from the washing, all with twins, and there is none barren among them.
text_la: Dentes tui sicut greges tonsarum quæ ascenderunt de lavacro; omnes gemellis fœtibus, et sterilis non est inter eas.
text_pt: Os teus dentes são como o rebanho das ovelhas tosquiadas, que sobem do lavadouro, e das quais todas produzem gêmeos, e nenhuma há estéril entre elas.
text_el: ὀδόντες σου ὡς ἀγέλαι τῶν κεκαρμένων αἳ ἀνέβησαν ἀπὸ τοῦ λουτροῦ αἱ πᾶσαι διδυμεύουσαι καὶ ἀτεκνοῦσα οὐκ ἔστιν ἐν αὐταῖς

text_en: Your lips are as a scarlet lace: and your speech sweet. Your cheeks are as a piece of a pomegranate, besides that which lies hid within.
text_la: Sicut vitta coccinea labia tua, et eloquium tuum dulce. Sicut fragmen mali punici, ita genæ tuæ, absque eo quod intrinsecus latet.
text_pt: Os teus lábios são como um fio de escarlate, e o teu falar é agradável; a tua fronte é qual um pedaço de romã entre os teus cabelos.
text_el: ὡς σπαρτίον τὸ κόκκινον χείλη σου καὶ ἡ λαλιά σου ὡραία ὡς λέπυρον τῆς ῥόας μῆλόν σου ἐκτὸς τῆς σιωπήσεώς σου

text_en: Your neck, is as the tower of David, which is built with bulwarks: a thousand bucklers hang upon it, all the armour of valiant men .
text_la: Sicut turris David collum tuum, quæ ædificata est cum propugnaculis; mille clypei pendent ex ea, omnis armatura fortium.
text_pt: O teu pescoço é como a torre de Davi, edificada para pendurar armas; mil escudos pendem dela, todos broquéis de poderosos.
text_el: ὡς πύργος Δαυιδ τράχηλός σου ὁ ᾠκοδομημένος εἰς θαλπιωθ χίλιοι θυρεοὶ κρέμανται ἐπ' αὐτόν πᾶσαι βολίδες τῶν δυνατῶν

text_en: Your two breasts like two young roes that are twins, which feed among the lilies.
text_la: Duo ubera tua sicut duo hinnuli, capreæ gemelli, qui pascuntur in liliis.
text_pt: Os teus dois seios são como dois filhos gêmeos da gazela, que se apascentam entre os lírios.
text_el: δύο μαστοί σου ὡς δύο νεβροὶ δίδυμοι δορκάδος οἱ νεμόμενοι ἐν κρίνοις

text_en: Till the day break, and the shadows retire, I will go to the mountain of myrrh, and to the hill of frankincense.
text_la: Donec aspiret dies, et inclinentur umbræ, vadam ad montem myrrhæ, et ad collem thuris.
text_pt: Até que refresque o dia, e fujam as sombras, irei ao monte da mirra, e ao outeiro do incenso.
text_el: ἕως οὗ διαπνεύσῃ ἡ ἡμέρα καὶ κινηθῶσιν αἱ σκιαί πορεύσομαι ἐμαυτῷ πρὸς τὸ ὄρος τῆς σμύρνης καὶ πρὸς τὸν βουνὸν τοῦ Λιβάνου

text_en: You are all fair, O my love , and there is not a spot in you.
text_la: Tota pulchra es, amica mea, et macula non est in te.
text_pt: Tu és toda formosa, meu amor, e em ti não há mancha.
text_el: ὅλη καλὴ εἶ ἡ πλησίον μου καὶ μῶμος οὐκ ἔστιν ἐν σοί

text_en: Come from Libanus , my spouse, come from Libanus , come: you shall be crowned from the top of Amana, from the top of Sanir and Hermon , from the dens of the lions, from the mountains of the leopards.
text_la: Veni de Libano, sponsa mea : veni de Libano, veni, coronaberis : de capite Amana, de vertice Sanir et Hermon, de cubilibus leonum, de montibus pardorum.
text_pt: Vem comigo do Líbano, ó minha esposa, vem comigo do Líbano; olha desde o cume de Amana, desde o cume de Senir e de Hermom, desde os covis dos leões, desde os montes dos leopardos.
text_el: δεῦρο ἀπὸ Λιβάνου νύμφη δεῦρο ἀπὸ Λιβάνου ἐλεύσῃ καὶ διελεύσῃ ἀπὸ ἀρχῆς πίστεως ἀπὸ κεφαλῆς Σανιρ καὶ Ερμων ἀπὸ μανδρῶν λεόντων ἀπὸ ὀρέων παρδάλεων

text_en: You have wounded my heart, my sister, my spouse, you have wounded my heart with one of your eyes, and with one hair of your neck.
text_la: Vulnerasti cor meum, soror mea, sponsa; vulnerasti cor meum in uno oculorum tuorum, et in uno crine colli tui.
text_pt: Enlevaste-me o coração, minha irmã, minha esposa; enlevaste-me o coração com um dos teus olhares, com um colar do teu pescoço.
text_el: ἐκαρδίωσας ἡμᾶς ἀδελφή μου νύμφη ἐκαρδίωσας ἡμᾶς ἑνὶ ἀπὸ ὀφθαλμῶν σου ἐν μιᾷ ἐνθέματι τραχήλων σου

text_en: How beautiful are your breasts, my sister, my spouse! your breasts are more beautiful than wine, and the sweet smell of your ointments above all aromatical spices.
text_la: Quam pulchræ sunt mammæ tuæ, soror mea sponsa! pulchriora sunt ubera tua vino, et odor unguentorum tuorum super omnia aromata.
text_pt: Que belos são os teus amores, minha irmã, esposa minha! Quanto melhor é o teu amor do que o vinho! E o aroma dos teus ungüentos do que o de todas as especiarias!
text_el: τί ἐκαλλιώθησαν μαστοί σου ἀδελφή μου νύμφη τί ἐκαλλιώθησαν μαστοί σου ἀπὸ οἴνου καὶ ὀσμὴ ἱματίων σου ὑπὲρ πάντα τὰ ἀρώματα

text_en: Your lips, my spouse, are as a dropping honeycomb, honey and milk are under your tongue; and the smell of your garments, as the smell of frankincense.
text_la: Favus distillans labia tua, sponsa; mel et lac sub lingua tua : et odor vestimentorum tuorum sicut odor thuris.
text_pt: Favos de mel manam dos teus lábios, minha esposa! Mel e leite estão debaixo da tua língua, e o cheiro dos teus vestidos é como o cheiro do Líbano.
text_el: κηρίον ἀποστάζουσιν χείλη σου νύμφη μέλι καὶ γάλα ὑπὸ τὴν γλῶσσάν σου καὶ ὀσμὴ ἱματίων σου ὡς ὀσμὴ Λιβάνου

text_en: My sister, my spouse, is a garden enclosed, a garden enclosed, a fountain sealed up.
text_la: Hortus conclusus soror mea, sponsa, hortus conclusus, fons signatus.
text_pt: Jardim fechado és tu, minha irmã, esposa minha, manancial fechado, fonte selada.
text_el: κῆπος κεκλεισμένος ἀδελφή μου νύμφη κῆπος κεκλεισμένος πηγὴ ἐσφραγισμένη

text_en: Your plants are a paradise of pomegranates with the fruits of the orchard. Cypress with spikenard.
text_la: Emissiones tuæ paradisus malorum punicorum, cum pomorum fructibus, cypri cum nardo.
text_pt: Os teus renovos são um pomar de romãs, com frutos excelentes, o cipreste com o nardo.
text_el: ἀποστολαί σου παράδεισος ῥοῶν μετὰ καρποῦ ἀκροδρύων κύπροι μετὰ νάρδων

text_en: Spikenard and saffron, sweet cane and cinnamon, with all the trees of Libanus, myrrh and aloes with all the chief perfumes.
text_la: Nardus et crocus, fistula et cinnamomum, cum universis lignis Libani; myrrha et aloë, cum omnibus primis unguentis.
text_pt: O nardo, e o açafrão, o cálamo, e a canela, com toda a sorte de árvores de incenso, a mirra e aloés, com todas as principais especiarias.
text_el: νάρδος καὶ κρόκος κάλαμος καὶ κιννάμωμον μετὰ πάντων ξύλων τοῦ Λιβάνου σμύρνα αλωθ μετὰ πάντων πρώτων μύρων

text_en: The fountain of gardens: the well of living waters, which run with a strong stream from Libanus.
text_la: Fons hortorum, puteus aquarum viventium, quæ fluunt impetu de Libano.
text_pt: És a fonte dos jardins, poço das águas vivas, que correm do Líbano!
text_el: πηγὴ κήπων φρέαρ ὕδατος ζῶντος καὶ ῥοιζοῦντος ἀπὸ τοῦ Λιβάνου

text_en: Arise, O north wind, and come, O south wind, blow through my garden, and let the aromatical spices thereof flow.
text_la: Sponsa. Surge, aquilo, et veni, auster : perfla hortum meum, et fluant aromata illius.
text_pt: Levanta-te, vento norte, e vem tu, vento sul; assopra no meu jardim, para que destilem os seus aromas. Ah! entre o meu amado no jardim, e coma os seus frutos excelentes!
text_el: ἐξεγέρθητι βορρᾶ καὶ ἔρχου νότε διάπνευσον κῆπόν μου καὶ ῥευσάτωσαν ἀρώματά μου καταβήτω ἀδελφιδός μου εἰς κῆπον αὐτοῦ καὶ φαγέτω καρπὸν ἀκροδρύων αὐτοῦ

text_en: Let my beloved come into his garden, and eat the fruit of his apple trees. I have come into my garden, O my sister, my spouse, I have gathered my myrrh, with my aromatical spices: I have eaten the honeycomb with my honey, I have drunk my wine with my milk: eat, O friends, and drink, and be inebriated, my dearly beloved.
text_la: Veniat dilectus meus in hortum suum, et comedat fructum pomorum suorum. Sponsus. Veni in hortum meum, soror mea, sponsa; messui myrrham meam cum aromatibus meis; comedi favum cum melle meo; bibi vinum meum cum lacte meo; comedite, amici, et bibite, et inebriamini, carissimi.
text_pt: Já entrei no meu jardim, minha irmã, minha esposa; colhi a minha mirra com a minha especiaria, comi o meu favo com o meu mel, bebi o meu vinho com o meu leite; comei, amigos, bebei abundantemente, ó amados.
text_el: εἰσῆλθον εἰς κῆπόν μου ἀδελφή μου νύμφη ἐτρύγησα σμύρναν μου μετὰ ἀρωμάτων μου ἔφαγον ἄρτον μου μετὰ μέλιτός μου ἔπιον οἶνόν μου μετὰ γάλακτός μου φάγετε πλησίοι καὶ πίετε καὶ μεθύσθητε ἀδελφοί

text_en: I sleep, and my heart watches: the voice of my beloved knocking: Open to me, my sister, my love , my dove , my undefiled: for my head is full of dew, and my locks of the drops of the nights.
text_la: Sponsa. Ego dormio, et cor meum vigilat. Vox dilecti mei pulsantis : Sponsus. Aperi mihi, soror mea, amica mea, columba mea, immaculata mea, quia caput meum plenum est rore, et cincinni mei guttis noctium.
text_pt: Eu dormia, mas o meu coração velava; e eis a voz do meu amado que está batendo: abre-me, minha irmã, meu amor, pomba minha, imaculada minha, porque a minha cabeça está cheia de orvalho, os meus cabelos das gotas da noite.
text_el: ἐγὼ καθεύδω καὶ ἡ καρδία μου ἀγρυπνεῖ φωνὴ ἀδελφιδοῦ μου κρούει ἐπὶ τὴν θύραν ἄνοιξόν μοι ἀδελφή μου ἡ πλησίον μου περιστερά μου τελεία μου ὅτι ἡ κεφαλή μου ἐπλήσθη δρόσου καὶ οἱ βόστρυχοί μου ψεκάδων νυκτός

text_en: I have put off my garment, how shall I put it on? I have washed my feet , how shall I defile them?
text_la: Sponsa. Expoliavi me tunica mea : quomodo induar illa? lavi pedes meos : quomodo inquinabo illos?
text_pt: Já despi a minha roupa; como a tornarei a vestir? Já lavei os meus pés; como os tornarei a sujar?
text_el: ἐξεδυσάμην τὸν χιτῶνά μου πῶς ἐνδύσωμαι αὐτόν ἐνιψάμην τοὺς πόδας μου πῶς μολυνῶ αὐτούς

text_en: My beloved put his hand through the key hole, and my bowels were moved at his touch.
text_la: Dilectus meus misit manum suam per foramen, et venter meus intremuit ad tactum ejus.
text_pt: O meu amado pôs a sua mão pela fresta da porta, e as minhas entranhas estremeceram por amor dele.
text_el: ἀδελφιδός μου ἀπέστειλεν χεῖρα αὐτοῦ ἀπὸ τῆς ὀπῆς καὶ ἡ κοιλία μου ἐθροήθη ἐπ' αὐτόν

text_en: I arose up to open to my beloved: my hands dropped with myrrh, and my fingers were full of the choicest myrrh.
text_la: Surrexi ut aperirem dilecto meo; manus meæ stillaverunt myrrham, et digiti mei pleni myrrha probatissima.
text_pt: Eu me levantei para abrir ao meu amado, e as minhas mãos gotejavam mirra, e os meus dedos mirra com doce aroma, sobre as aldravas da fechadura.
text_el: ἀνέστην ἐγὼ ἀνοῖξαι τῷ ἀδελφιδῷ μου χεῖρές μου ἔσταξαν σμύρναν δάκτυλοί μου σμύρναν πλήρη ἐπὶ χεῖρας τοῦ κλείθρου

text_en: I opened the bolt of my door to my beloved: but he had turned aside, and was gone. My soul melted when he spoke: I sought him, and found him not: I called, and he did not answer me.
text_la: Pessulum ostii mei aperui dilecto meo, at ille declinaverat, atque transierat. Anima mea liquefacta est, ut locutus est; quæsivi, et non inveni illum; vocavi, et non respondit mihi.
text_pt: Eu abri ao meu amado, mas já o meu amado tinha se retirado, e tinha ido; a minha alma desfaleceu quando ele falou; busquei-o e não o achei, chamei-o e não me respondeu.
text_el: ἤνοιξα ἐγὼ τῷ ἀδελφιδῷ μου ἀδελφιδός μου παρῆλθεν ψυχή μου ἐξῆλθεν ἐν λόγῳ αὐτοῦ ἐζήτησα αὐτὸν καὶ οὐχ εὗρον αὐτόν ἐκάλεσα αὐτόν καὶ οὐχ ὑπήκουσέν μου

text_en: The keepers that go about the city found me: they struck me: and wounded me: the keepers of the walls took away my veil from me.
text_la: Invenerunt me custodes qui circumeunt civitatem; percusserunt me, et vulneraverunt me. Tulerunt pallium meum mihi custodes murorum.
text_pt: Acharam-me os guardas que rondavam pela cidade; espancaram-me, feriram-me, tiraram-me o manto os guardas dos muros.
text_el: εὕροσάν με οἱ φύλακες οἱ κυκλοῦντες ἐν τῇ πόλει ἐπάταξάν με ἐτραυμάτισάν με ἦραν τὸ θέριστρόν μου ἀπ' ἐμοῦ φύλακες τῶν τειχέων

text_en: I adjure you, O daughters of Jerusalem , if you find my beloved, that you tell him that I languish with love .
text_la: Adjuro vos, filiæ Jerusalem, si inveneritis dilectum meum, ut nuntietis ei quia amore langueo.
text_pt: Conjuro-vos, ó filhas de Jerusalém, que, se achardes o meu amado, lhe digais que estou enferma de amor.
text_el: ὥρκισα ὑμᾶς θυγατέρες Ιερουσαλημ ἐν ταῖς δυνάμεσιν καὶ ἐν ταῖς ἰσχύσεσιν τοῦ ἀγροῦ ἐὰν εὕρητε τὸν ἀδελφιδόν μου τί ἀπαγγείλητε αὐτῷ ὅτι τετρωμένη ἀγάπης εἰμὶ ἐγώ

text_en: What manner of one is your beloved of the beloved, O you most beautiful among women ? What manner of one is your beloved of the beloved, that you have so adjured us?
text_la: Chorus. Qualis est dilectus tuus ex dilecto, o pulcherrima mulierum? qualis est dilectus tuus ex dilecto, quia sic adjurasti nos?
text_pt: Que é o teu amado mais do que outro amado, ó tu, a mais formosa entre as mulheres? Que é o teu amado mais do que outro amado, que tanto nos conjuras?
text_el: τί ἀδελφιδός σου ἀπὸ ἀδελφιδοῦ ἡ καλὴ ἐν γυναιξίν τί ἀδελφιδός σου ἀπὸ ἀδελφιδοῦ ὅτι οὕτως ὥρκισας ἡμᾶς

text_en: My beloved is white and ruddy, chosen out of thousands.
text_la: Sponsa. Dilectus meus candidus et rubicundus; electus ex millibus.
text_pt: O meu amado é branco e rosado; ele é o primeiro entre dez mil.
text_el: ἀδελφιδός μου λευκὸς καὶ πυρρός ἐκλελοχισμένος ἀπὸ μυριάδων

text_en: His head is as the finest gold: his locks as branches of palm trees, black as a raven.
text_la: Caput ejus aurum optimum; comæ ejus sicut elatæ palmarum, nigræ quasi corvus.
text_pt: A sua cabeça é como o ouro mais apurado, os seus cabelos são crespos, pretos como o corvo.
text_el: κεφαλὴ αὐτοῦ χρυσίον καὶ φαζ βόστρυχοι αὐτοῦ ἐλάται μέλανες ὡς κόραξ

text_en: His eyes as doves upon brooks of waters, which are washed with milk, and sit beside the plentiful streams.
text_la: Oculi ejus sicut columbæ super rivulos aquarum, quæ lacte sunt lotæ, et resident juxta fluenta plenissima.
text_pt: Os seus olhos são como os das pombas junto às correntes das águas, lavados em leite, postos em engaste.
text_el: ὀφθαλμοὶ αὐτοῦ ὡς περιστεραὶ ἐπὶ πληρώματα ὑδάτων λελουσμέναι ἐν γάλακτι καθήμεναι ἐπὶ πληρώματα ὑδάτων

text_en: His cheeks are as beds of aromatical spices set by the perfumers. His lips are as lilies dropping choice myrrh.
text_la: Genæ illius sicut areolæ aromatum, consitæ a pigmentariis. Labia ejus lilia, distillantia myrrham primam.
text_pt: As suas faces são como um canteiro de bálsamo, como flores perfumadas; os seus lábios são como lírios gotejando mirra com doce aroma.
text_el: σιαγόνες αὐτοῦ ὡς φιάλαι τοῦ ἀρώματος φύουσαι μυρεψικά χείλη αὐτοῦ κρίνα στάζοντα σμύρναν πλήρη

text_en: His hands are turned and as of gold, full of hyacinths. His belly as of ivory, set with sapphires.
text_la: Manus illius tornatiles, aureæ, plenæ hyacinthis. Venter ejus eburneus, distinctus sapphiris.
text_pt: As suas mãos são como anéis de ouro engastados de berilo; o seu ventre como alvo marfim, coberto de safiras.
text_el: χεῖρες αὐτοῦ τορευταὶ χρυσαῖ πεπληρωμέναι θαρσις κοιλία αὐτοῦ πυξίον ἐλεφάντινον ἐπὶ λίθου σαπφείρου

text_en: His legs as pillars of marble, that are set upon bases of gold. His form as of Libanus , excellent as the cedars .
text_la: Crura illius columnæ marmoreæ quæ fundatæ sunt super bases aureas. Species ejus ut Libani, electus ut cedri.
text_pt: As suas pernas como colunas de mármore, colocadas sobre bases de ouro puro; o seu aspecto como o Líbano, excelente como os cedros.
text_el: κνῆμαι αὐτοῦ στῦλοι μαρμάρινοι τεθεμελιωμένοι ἐπὶ βάσεις χρυσᾶς εἶδος αὐτοῦ ὡς Λίβανος ἐκλεκτὸς ὡς κέδροι

text_en: His throat most sweet, and he is all lovely: such is my beloved, and he is my friend, O you daughters of Jerusalem .
text_la: Guttur illius suavissimum, et totus desiderabilis. Talis est dilectus meus, et ipse est amicus meus, filiæ Jerusalem.
text_pt: A sua boca é muitíssimo suave; sim, ele é totalmente desejável. Tal é o meu amado, e tal o meu amigo, ó filhas de Jerusalém.
text_el: φάρυγξ αὐτοῦ γλυκασμοὶ καὶ ὅλος ἐπιθυμία οὗτος ἀδελφιδός μου καὶ οὗτος πλησίον μου θυγατέρες Ιερουσαλημ

text_en: Whither is your beloved gone, O you most beautiful among women ? Whither is your beloved turned aside, and we will seek him with you?
text_la: Chorus. Quo abiit dilectus tuus, o pulcherrima mulierum? quo declinavit dilectus tuus? et quæremus eum tecum.
text_pt: Para onde foi o teu amado, ó mais formosa entre as mulheres? Para onde se retirou o teu amado, para que o busquemos contigo?
text_el: ποῦ ἀπῆλθεν ὁ ἀδελφιδός σου ἡ καλὴ ἐν γυναιξίν ποῦ ἀπέβλεψεν ὁ ἀδελφιδός σου καὶ ζητήσομεν αὐτὸν μετὰ σοῦ

text_en: My beloved has gone down into his garden, to the bed of aromatical spices, to feed in the gardens, and to gather lilies.
text_la: Sponsa. Dilectus meus descendit in hortum suum ad areolam aromatum, ut pascatur in hortis, et lilia colligat.
text_pt: O meu amado desceu ao seu jardim, aos canteiros de bálsamo, para apascentar nos jardins e para colher os lírios.
text_el: ἀδελφιδός μου κατέβη εἰς κῆπον αὐτοῦ εἰς φιάλας τοῦ ἀρώματος ποιμαίνειν ἐν κήποις καὶ συλλέγειν κρίνα

text_en: I to my beloved, and my beloved to me, who feeds among the lilies.
text_la: Ego dilecto meo, et dilectus meus mihi, qui pascitur inter lilia.
text_pt: Eu sou do meu amado, e o meu amado é meu;ele apascenta entre os lírios.
text_el: ἐγὼ τῷ ἀδελφιδῷ μου καὶ ἀδελφιδός μου ἐμοὶ ὁ ποιμαίνων ἐν τοῖς κρίνοις

text_en: You are beautiful, O my love , sweet and comely as Jerusalem terrible as an army set in array.
text_la: Sponsus. Pulchra es, amica mea; suavis, et decora sicut Jerusalem; terribilis ut castrorum acies ordinata.
text_pt: Formosa és, meu amor, como Tirza, aprazível como Jerusalém, terrível como um exército com bandeiras.
text_el: καλὴ εἶ ἡ πλησίον μου ὡς εὐδοκία ὡραία ὡς Ιερουσαλημ θάμβος ὡς τεταγμέναι

text_en: Turn away your eyes from me, for they have made me flee away. Your hair is as a flock of goats, that appear from Galaad.
text_la: Averte oculos tuos a me, quia ipsi me avolare fecerunt. Capilli tui sicut grex caprarum quæ apparuerunt de Galaad.
text_pt: Desvia de mim os teus olhos, porque eles me dominam. O teu cabelo é como o rebanho das cabras que aparecem em Gileade.
text_el: ἀπόστρεψον ὀφθαλμούς σου ἀπεναντίον μου ὅτι αὐτοὶ ἀνεπτέρωσάν με τρίχωμά σου ὡς ἀγέλαι τῶν αἰγῶν αἳ ἀνεφάνησαν ἀπὸ τοῦ Γαλααδ

text_en: Your teeth as a flock of sheep, which come up from the washing, all with twins, and there is none barren among them.
text_la: Dentes tui sicut grex ovium quæ ascenderunt de lavacro : omnes gemellis fœtibus, et sterilis non est in eis.
text_pt: Os teus dentes são como o rebanho de ovelhas que sobem do lavadouro, e das quais todas produzem gêmeos, e não há estéril entre elas.
text_el: ὀδόντες σου ὡς ἀγέλαι τῶν κεκαρμένων αἳ ἀνέβησαν ἀπὸ τοῦ λουτροῦ αἱ πᾶσαι διδυμεύουσαι καὶ ἀτεκνοῦσα οὐκ ἔστιν ἐν αὐταῖς

text_en: Your cheeks are as the bark of a pomegranate, beside what is hidden within you.
text_la: Sicut cortex mali punici, sic genæ tuæ, absque occultis tuis.
text_pt: Como um pedaço de romã, assim são as tuas faces entre os teus cabelos.
text_el: ὡς σπαρτίον τὸ κόκκινον χείλη σου καὶ ἡ λαλιά σου ὡραία ὡς λέπυρον τῆς ῥόας μῆλόν σου ἐκτὸς τῆς σιωπήσεώς σου

text_en: There are threescore queens, and fourscore concubines , and young maidens without number.
text_la: Sexaginta sunt reginæ, et octoginta concubinæ, et adolescentularum non est numerus.
text_pt: Sessenta são as rainhas, e oitenta as concubinas, e as virgens sem número.
text_el: ἑξήκοντά εἰσιν βασίλισσαι καὶ ὀγδοήκοντα παλλακαί καὶ νεάνιδες ὧν οὐκ ἔστιν ἀριθμός

text_en: One is my dove , my perfect one is but one, she is the only one of her mother, the chosen of her that bore her. The daughters saw her, and declared her most blessed : the queens and concubines , and they praised her.
text_la: Una est columba mea, perfecta mea, una est matris suæ, electa genetrici suæ. Viderunt eam filiæ, et beatissimam prædicaverunt; reginæ et concubinæ, et laudaverunt eam.
text_pt: Porém uma é a minha pomba, a minha imaculada, a única de sua mãe, e a mais querida daquela que a deu à luz; viram-na as filhas e chamaram-na bem-aventurada, as rainhas e as concubinas louvaram-na.
text_el: μία ἐστὶν περιστερά μου τελεία μου μία ἐστὶν τῇ μητρὶ αὐτῆς ἐκλεκτή ἐστιν τῇ τεκούσῃ αὐτῆς εἴδοσαν αὐτὴν θυγατέρες καὶ μακαριοῦσιν αὐτήν βασίλισσαι καὶ παλλακαὶ καὶ αἰνέσουσιν αὐτήν

text_en: Who is she that comes forth as the morning rising, fair as the moon, bright as the sun, terrible as an army set in array?
text_la: Quæ est ista quæ progreditur quasi aurora consurgens, pulchra ut luna, electa ut sol, terribilis ut castrorum acies ordinata?
text_pt: Quem é esta que aparece como a alva do dia, formosa como a lua, brilhante como o sol, terrível como um exército com bandeiras?
text_el: τίς αὕτη ἡ ἐκκύπτουσα ὡσεὶ ὄρθρος καλὴ ὡς σελήνη ἐκλεκτὴ ὡς ὁ ἥλιος θάμβος ὡς τεταγμέναι

text_en: I went down into the garden of nuts, to see the fruits of the valleys, and to look if the vineyard had flourished, and the pomegranates budded.
text_la: Sponsa. Descendi in hortum nucum, ut viderem poma convallium, et inspicerem si floruisset vinea, et germinassent mala punica.
text_pt: Desci ao jardim das nogueiras, para ver os frutos do vale, a ver se floresciam as vides e brotavam as romãzeiras.
text_el: εἰς κῆπον καρύας κατέβην ἰδεῖν ἐν γενήμασιν τοῦ χειμάρρου ἰδεῖν εἰ ἤνθησεν ἡ ἄμπελος ἐξήνθησαν αἱ ῥόαι ἐκεῖ δώσω τοὺς μαστούς μου σοί

text_en: I knew not: my soul troubled me for the chariots of Aminadab.
text_la: Nescivi : anima mea conturbavit me, propter quadrigas Aminadab.
text_pt: Antes de eu o sentir, me pôs a minha alma nos carros do meu nobre povo.
text_el: οὐκ ἔγνω ἡ ψυχή μου ἔθετό με ἅρματα Αμιναδαβ

text_en: Return, return, O Sulamitess: return, return that we may behold you.
text_la: Chorus. Revertere, revertere, Sulamitis! revertere, revertere ut intueamur te.
text_pt: Quão formosos são os teus pés nos sapatos, ó filha do príncipe! Os contornos de tuas coxas são como jóias, trabalhadas por mãos de artista.
text_el: ἐπίστρεφε ἐπίστρεφε ἡ Σουλαμῖτις ἐπίστρεφε ἐπίστρεφε καὶ ὀψόμεθα ἐν σοί τί ὄψεσθε ἐν τῇ Σουλαμίτιδι ἡ ἐρχομένη ὡς χοροὶ τῶν παρεμβολῶν

text_en: What shall you see in the Sulamitess but the companies of camps? How beautiful are your steps in shoes, O prince's daughter! The joints of your thighs are like jewels , that are made by the hand of a skilful workman.
text_la: Sponsa. Quid videbis in Sulamite, nisi choros castrorum? Chorus. Quam pulchri sunt gressus tui in calceamentis, filia principis! Juncturæ femorum tuorum sicut monilia quæ fabricata sunt manu artificis.
text_pt: O teu umbigo como uma taça redonda, a que não falta bebida; o teu ventre como montão de trigo, cercado de lírios.
text_el: τί ὡραιώθησαν διαβήματά σου ἐν ὑποδήμασιν θύγατερ Ναδαβ ῥυθμοὶ μηρῶν σου ὅμοιοι ὁρμίσκοις ἔργῳ χειρῶν τεχνίτου

text_en: Your navel is like a round bowl never wanting cups. Your belly is like a heap of wheat, set about with lilies.
text_la: Umbilicus tuus crater tornatilis, numquam indigens poculis. Venter tuus sicut acervus tritici vallatus liliis.
text_pt: Os teus dois seios como dois filhos gêmeos de gazela.
text_el: ὀμφαλός σου κρατὴρ τορευτὸς μὴ ὑστερούμενος κρᾶμα κοιλία σου θιμωνιὰ σίτου πεφραγμένη ἐν κρίνοις

text_en: Your two breasts are like two young roes that are twins.
text_la: Duo ubera tua sicut duo hinnuli, gemelli capreæ.
text_pt: O teu pescoço como a torre de marfim; os teus olhos como as piscinas de Hesbom, junto à porta de Bate-Rabim; o teu nariz como torre do Líbano, que olha para Damasco.
text_el: δύο μαστοί σου ὡς δύο νεβροὶ δίδυμοι δορκάδος

text_en: Your neck as a tower of ivory . Your eyes like the fishpools in Hesebon , which are in the gate of the daughter of the multitude. Your nose is as the tower of Libanus, that looks toward Damascus .
text_la: Collum tuum sicut turris eburnea; oculi tui sicut piscinæ in Hesebon quæ sunt in porta filiæ multitudinis. Nasus tuus sicut turris Libani, quæ respicit contra Damascum.
text_pt: A tua cabeça sobre ti é como o monte Carmelo, e os cabelos da tua cabeça como a púrpura; o rei está preso nas galerias.
text_el: τράχηλός σου ὡς πύργος ἐλεφάντινος ὀφθαλμοί σου ὡς λίμναι ἐν Εσεβων ἐν πύλαις θυγατρὸς πολλῶν μυκτήρ σου ὡς πύργος τοῦ Λιβάνου σκοπεύων πρόσωπον Δαμασκοῦ

text_en: Your head is like Carmel : and the hairs of your head as the purple of the king bound in the channels.
text_la: Caput tuum ut Carmelus; et comæ capitis tui sicut purpura regis vincta canalibus.
text_pt: Quão formosa, e quão aprazível és, ó amor em delícias!
text_el: κεφαλή σου ἐπὶ σὲ ὡς Κάρμηλος καὶ πλόκιον κεφαλῆς σου ὡς πορφύρα βασιλεὺς δεδεμένος ἐν παραδρομαῖς

text_en: How beautiful are you, and how comely, my dearest, in delights!
text_la: Sponsus. Quam pulchra es, et quam decora, carissima, in deliciis!
text_pt: A tua estatura é semelhante à palmeira; e os teus seios são semelhantes aos cachos de uvas.
text_el: τί ὡραιώθης καὶ τί ἡδύνθης ἀγάπη ἐν τρυφαῖς σου

text_en: Your stature is like to a palm tree, and your breasts to clusters of grapes.
text_la: Statura tua assimilata est palmæ, et ubera tua botris.
text_pt: Dizia eu: Subirei à palmeira, pegarei em seus ramos; e então os teus seios serão como os cachos na vide, e o cheiro da tua respiração como o das maçãs.
text_el: τοῦτο μέγεθός σου ὡμοιώθη τῷ φοίνικι καὶ οἱ μαστοί σου τοῖς βότρυσιν

text_en: I said: I will go up into the palm tree, and will take hold of the fruit thereof: and your breasts shall be as the clusters of the vine: and the odour of your mouth like apples.
text_la: Dixi : Ascendam in palmam, et apprehendam fructus ejus; et erunt ubera tua sicut botri vineæ, et odor oris tui sicut malorum.
text_pt: E a tua boca como o bom vinho para o meu amado, que se bebe suavemente, e faz com que falem os lábios dos que dormem.
text_el: εἶπα ἀναβήσομαι ἐν τῷ φοίνικι κρατήσω τῶν ὕψεων αὐτοῦ καὶ ἔσονται δὴ μαστοί σου ὡς βότρυες τῆς ἀμπέλου καὶ ὀσμὴ ῥινός σου ὡς μῆλα

text_en: Your throat like the best wine, worthy for my beloved to drink, and for his lips and his teeth to ruminate.
text_la: Guttur tuum sicut vinum optimum, dignum dilecto meo ad potandum, labiisque et dentibus illius ad ruminandum.
text_pt: Eu sou do meu amado, e ele me tem afeição.
text_el: καὶ λάρυγξ σου ὡς οἶνος ὁ ἀγαθὸς πορευόμενος τῷ ἀδελφιδῷ μου εἰς εὐθύθητα ἱκανούμενος χείλεσίν μου καὶ ὀδοῦσιν

text_en: I to my beloved, and his turning is towards me.
text_la: Sponsa. Ego dilecto meo, et ad me conversio ejus.
text_pt: Vem, ó amado meu, saiamos ao campo, passemos as noites nas aldeias.
text_el: ἐγὼ τῷ ἀδελφιδῷ μου καὶ ἐπ' ἐμὲ ἡ ἐπιστροφὴ αὐτοῦ

text_en: Come, my beloved, let us go forth into the field, let us abide in the villages .
text_la: Veni, dilecte mi, egrediamur in agrum, commoremur in villis.
text_pt: Levantemo-nos de manhã para ir às vinhas, vejamos se florescem as vides, se já aparecem as tenras uvas, se já brotam as romãzeiras; ali te darei os meus amores.
text_el: ἐλθέ ἀδελφιδέ μου ἐξέλθωμεν εἰς ἀγρόν αὐλισθῶμεν ἐν κώμαις

text_en: Let us get up early to the vineyards, let us see if the vineyard flourish, if the flowers be ready to bring forth fruits, if the pomegranates flourish: there will I give you my breasts.
text_la: Mane surgamus ad vineas : videamus si floruit vinea, si flores fructus parturiunt, si floruerunt mala punica; ibi dabo tibi ubera mea.
text_pt: As mandrágoras exalam o seu perfume, e às nossas portas há todo o gênero de excelentes frutos, novos e velhos; ó amado meu, eu os guardei para ti.
text_el: ὀρθρίσωμεν εἰς ἀμπελῶνας ἴδωμεν εἰ ἤνθησεν ἡ ἄμπελος ἤνθησεν ὁ κυπρισμός ἤνθησαν αἱ ῥόαι ἐκεῖ δώσω τοὺς μαστούς μου σοί

text_en: The mandrakes give a smell. In our gates are all fruits: the new and the old, my beloved, I have kept for you.
text_la: Mandragoræ dederunt odorem in portis nostris omnia poma : nova et vetera, dilecte mi, servavi tibi.
text_el: οἱ μανδραγόραι ἔδωκαν ὀσμήν καὶ ἐπὶ θύραις ἡμῶν πάντα ἀκρόδρυα νέα πρὸς παλαιά ἀδελφιδέ μου ἐτήρησά σοι

text_en: Who shall give you to me for my brother, sucking the breasts of my mother, that I may find you without, and kiss you, and now no man may despise me?
text_la: Quis mihi det te fratrem meum, sugentem ubera matris meæ, ut inveniam te foris, et deosculer te, et jam me nemo despiciat?
text_pt: Ah! quem me dera que foras como meu irmão, que mamou aos seios de minha mãe! Quando te encontrasse lá fora, beijar-te-ia, e não me desprezariam!
text_el: τίς δῴη σε ἀδελφιδόν μου θηλάζοντα μαστοὺς μητρός μου εὑροῦσά σε ἔξω φιλήσω σε καί γε οὐκ ἐξουδενώσουσίν μοι

text_en: I will take hold of you, and bring you into my mother's house: there you shall teach me, and I will give you a cup of spiced wine and new wine of my pomegranates.
text_la: Apprehendam te, et ducam in domum matris meæ : ibi me docebis, et dabo tibi poculum ex vino condito, et mustum malorum granatorum meorum.
text_pt: Levar-te-ia e te introduziria na casa de minha mãe, e tu me ensinarias; eu te daria a beber do vinho aromático e do mosto das minhas romãs.
text_el: παραλήμψομαί σε εἰσάξω σε εἰς οἶκον μητρός μου καὶ εἰς ταμίειον τῆς συλλαβούσης με ποτιῶ σε ἀπὸ οἴνου τοῦ μυρεψικοῦ ἀπὸ νάματος ῥοῶν μου

text_en: His left hand under my head, and his right hand shall embrace me.
text_la: Læva ejus sub capite meo, et dextera illius amplexabitur me.
text_pt: A sua mão esquerda esteja debaixo da minha cabeça, e a sua direita me abrace.
text_el: εὐώνυμος αὐτοῦ ὑπὸ τὴν κεφαλήν μου καὶ ἡ δεξιὰ αὐτοῦ περιλήμψεταί με

text_en: I adjure you, O daughters of Jerusalem , that you stir not up, nor awake my love till she please.
text_la: Sponsus. Adjuro vos, filiæ Jerusalem, ne suscitetis, neque evigilare faciatis dilectam, donec ipsa velit.
text_pt: Conjuro-vos, ó filhas de Jerusalém, que não acordeis nem desperteis o meu amor, até que queira.
text_el: ὥρκισα ὑμᾶς θυγατέρες Ιερουσαλημ ἐν ταῖς δυνάμεσιν καὶ ἐν ταῖς ἰσχύσεσιν τοῦ ἀγροῦ τί ἐγείρητε καὶ τί ἐξεγείρητε τὴν ἀγάπην ἕως ἂν θελήσῃ

text_en: Who is this that comes up from the desert , flowing with delights, leaning upon her beloved? Under the apple tree I raised you up: there your mother was corrupted, there she was defloured that bore you.
text_la: Chorus. Quæ est ista quæ ascendit de deserto, deliciis affluens, innixa super dilectum suum? Sponsus. Sub arbore malo suscitavi te; ibi corrupta est mater tua, ibi violata est genitrix tua.
text_pt:
Quem é esta que sobe do deserto, e vem encostada ao seu amado?
Debaixo da macieira te despertei, ali esteve tua mãe com dores; ali esteve com dores aquela que te deu à luz.
text_el: τίς αὕτη ἡ ἀναβαίνουσα λελευκανθισμένη ἐπιστηριζομένη ἐπὶ τὸν ἀδελφιδὸν αὐτῆς ὑπὸ μῆλον ἐξήγειρά σε ἐκεῖ ὠδίνησέν σε ἡ μήτηρ σου ἐκεῖ ὠδίνησέν σε ἡ τεκοῦσά σου

text_en: Put me as a seal upon your heart, as a seal upon your arm, for love is strong as death, jealousy as hard as hell, the lamps thereof are fire and flames.
text_la: Sponsa. Pone me ut signaculum super cor tuum, ut signaculum super brachium tuum, quia fortis est ut mors dilectio, dura sicut infernus æmulatio : lampades ejus lampades ignis atque flammarum.
text_pt: Põe-me como selo sobre o teu coração, como selo sobre o teu braço, porque o amor é forte como a morte, e duro como a sepultura o ciúme; as suas brasas são brasas de fogo, com veementes labaredas.
text_el: θές με ὡς σφραγῖδα ἐπὶ τὴν καρδίαν σου ὡς σφραγῖδα ἐπὶ τὸν βραχίονά σου ὅτι κραταιὰ ὡς θάνατος ἀγάπη σκληρὸς ὡς ᾅδης ζῆλος περίπτερα αὐτῆς περίπτερα πυρός φλόγες αὐτῆς

text_en: Many waters cannot quench charity , neither can the floods drown it: if a man should give all the substance of his house for love , he shall despise it as nothing.
text_la: Aquæ multæ non potuerunt extinguere caritatem, nec flumina obruent illam. Si dederit homo omnem substantiam domus suæ pro dilectione, quasi nihil despiciet eam.
text_pt: As muitas águas não podem apagar este amor, nem os rios afogá-lo; ainda que alguém desse todos os bens de sua casa pelo amor, certamente o desprezariam.
text_el: ὕδωρ πολὺ οὐ δυνήσεται σβέσαι τὴν ἀγάπην καὶ ποταμοὶ οὐ συγκλύσουσιν αὐτήν ἐὰν δῷ ἀνὴρ τὸν πάντα βίον αὐτοῦ ἐν τῇ ἀγάπῃ ἐξουδενώσει ἐξουδενώσουσιν αὐτόν

text_en: Our sister is little, and has no breasts. What shall we do to our sister in the day when she is to be spoken to?
text_la: Chorus Fratrum. Soror nostra parva, et ubera non habet; quid faciemus sorori nostræ in die quando alloquenda est?
text_pt: Temos uma irmã pequena, que ainda não tem seios; que faremos a esta nossa irmã, no dia em que dela se falar?
text_el: ἀδελφὴ ἡμῖν μικρὰ καὶ μαστοὺς οὐκ ἔχει τί ποιήσωμεν τῇ ἀδελφῇ ἡμῶν ἐν ἡμέρᾳ ᾗ ἐὰν λαληθῇ ἐν αὐτῇ

text_en: If she be a wall: let us build upon it bulwarks of silver: if she be a door, let us join it together with boards of cedar .
text_la: Si murus est, ædificemus super eum propugnacula argentea; si ostium est, compingamus illud tabulis cedrinis.
text_pt: Se ela for um muro, edificaremos sobre ela um palácio de prata; e, se ela for uma porta, cercá-la-emos com tábuas de cedro.
text_el: εἰ τεῖχός ἐστιν οἰκοδομήσωμεν ἐπ' αὐτὴν ἐπάλξεις ἀργυρᾶς καὶ εἰ θύρα ἐστίν διαγράψωμεν ἐπ' αὐτὴν σανίδα κεδρίνην

text_en: I am a wall: and my breasts are as a tower since I have become in his presence as one finding peace.
text_la: Sponsa. Ego murus, et ubera mea sicut turris, ex quo facta sum coram eo, quasi pacem reperiens.
text_pt: Eu sou um muro, e os meus seios são como as suas torres; então eu era aos seus olhos como aquela que acha paz.
text_el: ἐγὼ τεῖχος καὶ μαστοί μου ὡς πύργοι ἐγὼ ἤμην ἐν ὀφθαλμοῖς αὐτοῦ ὡς εὑρίσκουσα εἰρήνην

text_en: The peaceable had a vineyard, in that which has people: he let out the same to keepers, every man brings for the fruit thereof a thousand pieces of silver.
text_la: Chorus Fratrum. Vinea fuit pacifico in ea quæ habet populos : tradidit eam custodibus; vir affert pro fructu ejus mille argenteos.
text_pt: Teve Salomão uma vinha em Baal-Hamom; entregou-a a uns guardas; e cada um lhe trazia pelo seu fruto mil peças de prata.
text_el: ἀμπελὼν ἐγενήθη τῷ Σαλωμων ἐν Βεελαμων ἔδωκεν τὸν ἀμπελῶνα αὐτοῦ τοῖς τηροῦσιν ἀνὴρ οἴσει ἐν καρπῷ αὐτοῦ χιλίους ἀργυρίου

text_en: My vineyard is before me. A thousand are for you, the peaceable, and two hundred for them that keep the fruit thereof.
text_la: Sponsa. Vinea mea coram me est. Mille tui pacifici, et ducenti his qui custodiunt fructus ejus.
text_pt: A minha vinha, que me pertence, está diante de mim; as mil peças de prata são para ti, ó Salomão, e duzentas para os que guardam o seu fruto.
text_el: ἀμπελών μου ἐμὸς ἐνώπιόν μου οἱ χίλιοι σοί Σαλωμων καὶ οἱ διακόσιοι τοῖς τηροῦσι τὸν καρπὸν αὐτοῦ

text_en: You that dwell in the gardens, the friends hearken: make me hear your voice.
text_la: Sponsus. Quæ habitas in hortis, amici auscultant; fac me audire vocem tuam.
text_pt: Ó tu, que habitas nos jardins, os companheiros estão atentos para ouvir a tua voz; faze-me, pois, também ouvi-la.
text_el: ὁ καθήμενος ἐν κήποις ἑταῖροι προσέχοντες τῇ φωνῇ σου ἀκούτισόν με

text_en: Flee away, O my beloved, and be like to the roe, and to the young hart upon the mountains of aromatical spices.
text_la: Sponsa. Fuge, dilecte mi, et assimilare capreæ, hinnuloque cervorum super montes aromatum.
text_pt: Vem depressa, amado meu, e faze-te semelhante ao gamo ou ao filho dos veados sobre os montes dos aromas.
text_el: φύγε ἀδελφιδέ μου καὶ ὁμοιώθητι τῇ δορκάδι ἢ τῷ νεβρῷ τῶν ἐλάφων ἐπὶ ὄρη ἀρωμάτων
